text:
Joe (Customer): Hey, we've got repeated duplicate chunks and double billing when our web client reconnects mid-stream. Happened ~3x today.

Sam (Support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro or logs? is this SSE or websocket?

Joe (Customer): SSE from browser. We start a stream POST /v1/streams, get a session token in X-Redwood-Session, then client drops (mobile), reconnects with same token + ?resume=true. On reconnect we sometimes get the last partial chunk again AND the final chunk duplicated. Billing shows 2 generations for 1 user action.

Sam (Support): Oof. Can you share a small timeline + headers? especially Idempotency-Key or any resume token values.

Joe (Customer): timeline & headers:
1) POST /v1/streams -> 200 OK headers:
   X-Redwood-Session: s_7f9a
   Idempotency-Key: none
2) stream emits chunk seq=0..5, client ack seq=3 then network blip, socket closes
3) client reconnects: GET /v1/streams?resume=true with X-Redwood-Session: s_7f9a
   server starts from seq=3 and re-emits chunk 3..5 plus final result (duplicate).

Logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T18:02:03Z] session=s_7f9a generator=g_42 start seq=0
[2026-03-17T18:02:10Z] session=s_7f9a ack=3
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] connection lost (client tcp close)
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] reconnect request resume=true session=s_7f9a
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] spawned generator=g_43 (resume path) for session=s_7f9a
[2026-03-17T18:02:11Z] emit chunk seq=3 from g_42
[2026-03-17T18:02:12Z] emit chunk seq=3 from g_43 <-- duplicate
[2026-03-17T18:02:12Z] emit final from g_42
[2026-03-17T18:02:13Z] emit final from g_43 <-- duplicate billed twice
```

Sam (Support): Thanks. That log line 'spawned generator=g_43 (resume path)' looks wrong — resume should continue existing generator g_42 or handoff cleanly, not create a second active generator.

Lina (CS): @Sam can you confirm if client was sending an Idempotency-Key? If not, short-term we can advise customers to provide Idempotency-Key per user action to dedupe server-side. Long-term we should dedupe on generator_id + generation_id.

Joe (Customer): We didn't set Idempotency-Key originally. Hard to change older clients quickly. Can you recommend a server-side mitigation?

Kai (Infra): From logs it looks like a race in the session handoff: when connection closes and reconnect arrives within the 'grace window', the old generator isn't fully GC'd and we spawn a new one for resume. Both proceed and both produce final output. Root cause candidate: resume logic treats resume as 'start new if previous not confirmed finished'. We'll need trace for the generator lifecycle and lease state.

Sam (Support): Can you escalate? This is causing billing complaints. Customer wants a credit and an ETA for fix.

Lina (CS): Escalating now. @Kai can you take a look and share a quick mitigation? Two options: 1) short-term: if reconnect && session has active generator, return 409 or a 'wait' response asking client to retry after backoff (prevents duplicate spawn), OR 2) server-side dedupe: attach generation_id to outputs and ignore duplicates if same generation_id already emitted for session.

Kai (Infra): For quick patch we can add a server-side guard: when handling resume, check active_generator_id for session; if active and last_ack_seq < active.start_seq, then attach a 'resume_block' for 2000ms and replay only after confirming active generator finished or ack progressed. That avoids spawning g_43 immediately. I'll prototype.

DeployBot: rolling out canary patch streaming/resume-guard to staging -> prod canaries (job #8857).

Sam (Support): Meanwhile I'll offer the customer a credit for the duplicate charges and suggest client workaround: send Idempotency-Key per user action and include last-ack-seq in reconnect header.

Joe (Customer): Appreciate it. We'll add Idempotency-Key ASAP, but please keep us posted on the fix. Can you also share hits/metrics so we can verify duplicates stop?

Lina (CS): Will do. Sam: collect session IDs and billing tx ids and I'll open the credit ticket. @Kai please post trace id when you have prototype.

Kai (Infra): ack. Prototype done locally, need trace logs to validate. If confirmed will hotfix to canary within 2h.

Sam (Support): Thanks all. I'll send a follow-up with steps we asked the customer to run to gather logs (curl + header examples) and open an internal incident with priority P2 for billing impact. :thumbsup:

Joe (Customer): Thanks — sending logs shortly.
